clue.text: Motorway certain to limit coming problem

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway, written here with I for the figure 1

indicators.note: to limit something is to hem it in on both sides, so one word encloses the other

parts.note: certain means sure
Advent is the season marking a coming or arrival

explanation.surface: A motorway seems certain to restrict some looming trouble for drivers.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is Britain's best-known motorway; the figure 1 is written as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: A misadventure is a mishap or piece of bad luck, so it is a kind of trouble.

clue.text: Fail to get this compiler's message

parts.note: to miss something is to fail to get it
the setter refers to themself; 'this compiler has' shortens to I've

explanation.surface: A setter complains that a note sent to them never arrived.
explanation.definitionFit: A missive is a letter or written communication, a formal word for something sent.

clue.text: Consume less: miss eating meal's starter

indicators.note: one word eating another takes it inside itself

parts.note: to skip something is to miss it out

indicators.note: the starter of a word is its opening letter, as a starter opens a meal

explanation.surface: Dieting advice: eat less by dropping the first course of a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eating' puts M, the first letter of 'meal's' signalled by 'starter', inside SKIP.
explanation.definitionFit: To skimp is to stint or economise, using less of something than is needed.

clue.text: Trusted broadcast includes current rubbish

indicators.note: includes means one piece holds another within it
broadcast seed is scattered about, so these letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: I is the physics symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A reliable radio programme somehow carries the latest junk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' rearranges TRUSTED to DETRTUS, and 'includes' puts I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Detritus is debris or waste matter left behind, a synonym for junk.

clue.text: Effect creating loud applause, thunderous initially

definitions.text: Effect creating loud applause, thunderous initially

indicators.note: initially means the opening letter of each of the preceding words is taken

explanation.surface: A performance whose impact draws loud, thunderous clapping.
explanation.definitionFit: Eclat is brilliant success or striking effect, the kind that earns acclaim from an audience.

clue.text: Performing music in empty tasteless bling?

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another
an emptied word has lost its contents, leaving just its outer letters

parts.note: rapping is a style of performing music, rhythmic speech over a beat

explanation.surface: A rap star performs in garish, vulgar jewellery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'empty' keeps only the first and last letters of 'tasteless'.
explanation.definitionFit: Trappings are outward adornments and accessories; flashy jewellery is one example, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Slow blast with Queen rising

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the letters are read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: blast and drat are both mild curses
ER is the royal cipher, Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: A royal ascends slowly, muttering an oath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns the whole of DRATER upwards, as this is a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To retard something is to slow or delay it, as a verb.

clue.text: Possibly Spitfire trail follows twist

indicators.note: follows means the first-named piece comes after the second

parts.note: to warp is to twist out of shape
a lane is a narrow track or path, like a trail

explanation.surface: A vapour trail behind a spiralling aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spitfire was a famous British fighter aircraft of the Second World War, an example of a military plane.

clue.text: Unwilling to wear Church attire

indicators.note: a wearer is wrapped in garments, so one piece wears the other around it

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
loth (or loath) means unwilling

explanation.surface: Someone reluctant to dress up for a service.
explanation.definitionFit: To attire someone is to dress them, both verbs for putting garments on.

clue.text: Bit unwell in cast in suffering

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another
letters that are suffering are knocked about, so they are rearranged

parts.note: unwell means ill

explanation.surface: An actor in a theatre company is poorly and in pain.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'in' is the container signal; the second is part of the anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A scintilla is a tiny trace or spark, a minute amount.

clue.text: Dog's bottom seen taking run

definitions.note: read as 'Dog is', a verb: to dog someone is to follow them

indicators.note: taking means holding the next piece inside

parts.note: a tail is the rear end seen on an animal
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A dog's rear end visible as it runs off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking' puts R inside TAIL. 'Dog' is the verb, with 's as 'is' linking it to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To trail someone is to follow or shadow them, the same as dogging them.

clue.text: Yours truly's beer, imbibing right brand

parts.note: yours truly means the speaker, and 'yours truly is' shortens to I'm

indicators.note: imbibing means drinking in, so one piece takes the other inside

parts.note: a pint is a glass of beer

explanation.surface: A drinker boasts of beer with a proper label.
explanation.definitionFit: An imprint is a mark or stamp left on something, as a brand is.

clue.text: Treasure having a box inside bank

indicators.note: inside means the pieces sit within another

parts.note: a pet is a treasured favourite
to box is to hit, as is to rap

explanation.surface: A treasure chest buried in a riverbank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having' is a link; to box someone's ears is to strike them.
explanation.definitionFit: A parapet is a low protective wall or earthwork, a defensive bank.

clue.text: Carrying out death penalty?

definitions.meaning: an ... of a plan is the performance or doing of it
the carrying out of a death sentence

explanation.definitionFit: Execution means both the performing of a task and the putting to death of a condemned person.

clue.text: Twisting a lever to lift

indicators.note: twisting distorts these words, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Operating a mechanism by turning a lever to raise something.
explanation.definitionFit: Lift is the British word for an elevator, the cage that carries people between floors.

clue.text: Dig tunnel somehow being patient

indicators.note: somehow means in some unspecified way, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Digging a tunnel slowly takes forbearance.
explanation.definitionFit: An indulgent person is tolerant and lenient, showing patience with others' faults.

clue.text: Curse sweetheart after embargo

indicators.note: after means the first-named piece comes second

parts.note: an embargo is a ban on trade
the heart of the word 'sweet' is its middle letter, E

explanation.surface: Bad luck for a lover whose romance is forbidden.
explanation.definitionFit: A bane is a curse or persistent cause of trouble.

clue.text: Illness keeping public upset for good

indicators.note: keeping means holding another piece inside

parts.note: a virus causes illness

indicators.note: in a down clue upset turns a word upside down, reading it backwards

parts.note: out means public, as in a secret being out

explanation.surface: A disease hidden from the public, distressing for all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' works only on the word for public; 'for' links wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Virtuous means morally upright, having goodness of character.

clue.text: Female ran and took off

parts.note: to run an organisation is to lead it, so ran gives led

explanation.surface: A woman ran and left.
explanation.definitionFit: Fled means ran away or escaped, the same as took off in the sense of departing hastily.

clue.text: Superficial account found in dossier

indicators.note: found in means a piece is located inside another

parts.note: a dossier is a file of documents

explanation.surface: A shallow report turns up in an intelligence file.
explanation.definitionFit: Facile means glib and shallow, lacking depth of thought.

clue.text: Detective's dispatched, checking identity for protester

parts.note: DI is a Detective Inspector, with the 's giving S

indicators.note: checking means holding back, so one piece stops the other inside it

parts.note: dispatched means sent
ID is short for identity

explanation.surface: A police officer is sent out to check papers of a demonstrator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'checking' acts like a restraint, holding the identity abbreviation within the word for dispatched.
explanation.definitionFit: A dissident opposes official policy, a protester against the regime.

clue.text: In part rest legs getting support

indicators.note: In means the answer is sitting inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Resting partly on legs, something is propped up.
explanation.definitionFit: A trestle is a framework of legs and a crossbar that holds up a table top.

clue.text: Doodle produced by small stroke

parts.note: the crawl is a swimming stroke

explanation.surface: A quick drawing made with one small pen stroke.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrawl is careless, hasty writing or drawing, much like a doodle.

clue.text: Risk with large section of church

parts.note: to chance something is to risk it

explanation.surface: A big gamble on one part of a church building.
explanation.definitionFit: The chancel is the part of a church near the altar, where clergy and choir sit.

clue.text: Enclosure surrounds extravagant country residence

indicators.note: surrounds means one piece goes around the other

parts.note: a cage is an enclosure
OTT, over the top, means extravagant

explanation.surface: A fence encircles a lavish house in the countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: A cottage is a small house, typically in the countryside.

clue.text: Throttle or carburettor part

definitions.meaning: a valve in a carburettor restricting air flow to enrich the fuel mixture

explanation.definitionFit: Choke means both to strangle someone and the device that limits air into an engine for cold starts.

clue.text: Defence of tabloid bait, occasionally

indicators.note: occasionally means only some letters, here every other one

explanation.surface: A sensational newspaper story used as a defence.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the second, fourth and so on letters of 'tabloid bait'.
explanation.definitionFit: An alibi is a plea that the accused was elsewhere when a crime happened, a legal defence.

clue.text: Sponge from a sucker taken aback

indicators.note: taken aback suggests going backwards, so these letters are read in reverse

parts.note: a sucker is a fool, someone easily duped

explanation.surface: An easily duped person is surprised by what they bought.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken aback' reverses A FOOL as a whole.
explanation.definitionFit: A loofa is a dried gourd used as a bath scrubber, a kind of sponge.

clue.text: Adjusting to income's for finance expert

indicators.note: adjusting means altering, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the possessive S is counted as a letter here, giving the word with S on the end

explanation.surface: Fine-tuning earnings is the work of a money expert.
explanation.definitionFit: An economist studies how money, production and trade work, an expert on finance.

clue.text: Chatterer thrashes with black bird outside

indicators.note: outside means these pieces go round another

parts.note: B is short for black, as on pencils
a kite is a bird of prey
to lather someone is to beat or thrash them

explanation.surface: A dark bird beats its wings around something.
explanation.walkthrough: B and KITE go either side of LATHERS.
explanation.definitionFit: A blatherskite is someone who talks long-windedly and foolishly, a chatterbox.
